title: Quentin and the Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1848, in the river city of Aldenmoor, Sebastian Vane works her late father's type-cutting bench in the Pemberton & Vane print shop, presenting as a young man to keep the trade she inherited. When the census taker, Quentin Ashe, notices the discrepancies in the household rolls and asks one question too many, Sebastian's fragile identity is exposed — but Quentin, a disgraced archivist with his own erased past, chooses to help rather than report her. As revolution sweeps the city and the print shop becomes a target for both sides, the two race to print a true record of the neighborhood's dead and displaced before the victors' historians can rewrite the ledger. The book ends with the presses running as soldiers breach the door, the truth already in a thousand hands, and Sebastian choosing to sign her own name to it at last.
about_author: G. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in the American Midwest. Their fiction is drawn from marginalia found in the ledgers of defunct print shops, where ordinary people left traces of lives the official record omitted.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A day in the print shop establishing her craft, her disguise, and the neighborhood that depends on her press. She cuts a new typeface for a funeral broadside, measuring grief in ems and picas. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness — everyone loves the shop, no one knows the hand behind it.

chapters.title: The Man with the Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The census taker works his rounds with mechanical detachment until he reaches Pemberton & Vane and finds a name that matches a boy who died years ago. He asks one question too many. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into something dangerous — for both of them.

chapters.title: What the Register Says
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She discovers Quentin has flagged her household record for investigation and prepares to flee, packing what can be carried. Her mother's memory and the type cases argue against leaving. Emotional beat: the terror of erasure — she has spent her life becoming unrecordable, and now it may cost her everything.

chapters.title: A Question of Records
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin confronts Sebastian privately, expecting a fraud; instead he finds a craftsman and a story that mirrors his own — he was struck from the university rolls for a crime he didn't commit. Emotional beat: recognition. He tears the flag from her file and asks for work at the press.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, weeks later. Quentin learns the trade badly but eagerly, and the shop takes on a second rhythm. Sebastian teaches him to set type; he teaches her what the archives hold about her father's suppressed political pamphlets. Emotional beat: found family forming over shared labor and shared secrets.

chapters.title: Bread and Barricades
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The city tips into unrest; grain prices spike, the garrison mutinies, and the neighborhood organizes. The print shop becomes an informal headquarters for pamphlets. Emotional beat: the intoxication and dread of history arriving at the doorstep.

chapters.title: The Historian's Apprentice
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin's old mentor, now attached to the provisional government, offers him rehabilitation in exchange for drafting the official account of the uprising — an account that will omit the neighborhood's dead. Emotional beat: temptation of respectability versus the memory of his own erasure.

chapters.title: Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The first deaths occur in the street fighting, and neighbors begin leaving scraps of paper at the shop: names of the fallen the authorities won't record. Sebastian resolves to print them. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the press as a reliquary.

chapters.title: The Censor's Visit
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A government censor inspects the shop and nearly discovers the memorial broadside hidden in the forme. Quentin bluffs, spending the last of his credibility. Emotional beat: the cost of complicity rising; he is now a fugitive in all but name.

chapters.title: My Father's Face
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A customer who knew her father looks too long at her and calls her by her birth name aloud in the shop. She neither confirms nor denies, but the disguise feels thinner. Emotional beat: identity as performance wearing against the grain of longing to be known.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The provisional government purges the municipal archives, burning records inconvenient to its narrative — including Quentin's own file, his last proof he ever existed officially. Emotional beat: rage and clarity; he understands the victors' historians are already writing, and time has run out.

chapters.title: Setting the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, night work. She and Quentin compose the true ledger — two hundred names, causes, dates — in secret, type set mirror-wise so only the press can read it. Emotional beat: sacred exhaustion; the most important edition of her life, printed for no profit and no permission.

chapters.title: Quentin's Confession
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He admits to Sebastian that his mentor's offer still stands and that part of him wanted his name restored by the very people erasing others. Sebastian's response — anger, then forgiveness — reframes his choice. Emotional beat: the found family tested and holding.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A neighbor's son, arrested and released, has traded the shop's secrets for bread. Soldiers are expected. Sebastian must decide whether to run with the ledger's plates or stay to print. Emotional beat: betrayal from within the family she built; the question of what memory is worth.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They pack the plates into two cases and split them — Quentin takes one toward the river, Sebastian keeps the other, planning to reprint from separate halves. Emotional beat: trust as an act of faith; each carries half the truth and half the risk.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Low Water
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin is stopped at the checkpoint; the plates are found. He claims sole authorship to protect the shop, and is taken. Emotional beat: sacrifice — the erased man volunteering for erasure, one last time, on purpose.

chapters.title: The Empty Bench
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She waits at the rendezvous that never fills, then learns of Quentin's arrest from the informer's stricken mother. Grief and fury; the neighborhood rallies, bringing her the remaining names. Emotional beat: the found family closing around her — she is no longer alone, even in loss.

chapters.title: The Victor's Draft
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, in custody. His mentor offers him a final bargain: sign the official history, be restored, live. Quentin reads the draft aloud and finds his neighbors' deaths rendered as 'isolated disturbances.' Emotional beat: the climax of conscience; he refuses and asks only for paper and ink.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Copies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. With borrowed presses across the district, the neighborhood printers run the true ledger overnight — a decentralized print run the government cannot suppress. Sebastian sets the final line: her own name, Sebastian Vane, as compositor. Emotional beat: triumph of the small and many; identity claimed, not concealed.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At dawn the broadsides appear on every door, and the crowd reads the names aloud in the square as troops assemble. The victors' narrative cracks — too many witnesses hold the same true record. Emotional beat: catharsis; memory made public and unownable.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Quentin is released in the government's retreat, and the two face the aftermath: the shop looted, the city changed, the mentor's history already a laughingstock. Emotional beat: quiet reconciliation; the cost tallied honestly, and worth it.

chapters.title: The First Proof
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue. Months later, the shop reopens under both their names. Sebastian cuts a new typeface — the Vane face — and pulls the first proof of a book that tells the whole story, hers included. Emotional beat: resolution; memory preserved, identity whole, family found.
